figures.caption: Figure 2: Different evaluation interfaces reshape apparent model quality. A: CBraMod layer profiles under five readouts. B–C: Final-layer readout gains and additional fixed-readout depth gains; task colors are shared with A. D: Average ranks across the three primary tasks under mean-pooled final-layer evaluation, final-layer readout selection, and fixed-readout depth selection.
Figure 3: Source-selected depth transfers across datasets. A: Source-selected layer probing minus Final layer probing. B: Source-selected layer probing minus random-layer expectation.

Figure 4: Source-defined task directions retain predictive utility after transfer. In task transfer: HMC to ISRUC sleep staging (n = 98). A: Augmentation of final-layer features with four sourcederived residual coordinates, compared with ordinary supervised coordinates. B: Performance after removing source-defined versus random directions and refitting the target classifier. Labels indicate paired gains or excess losses; whiskers denote 95% participant-bootstrap intervals. All analyses use source-fitted PCA200 features.
Table 2: Absolute scores (%) and within-task ranks in parentheses. BA: OpenBMI; AUROC: N170/N400. Readout is selected at the final layer, then depth is selected at that readout.
Table 3: Complete primary effects (percent, paired 95% intervals). Readout correction, fixed-readout depth utility, and joint interface utility remain separate quantities.

Table 4: Learned-family controls. Absolute scores are percentages; selected-minus-final gains are expressed in percent with paired 95% intervals. Seeds are averaged within participant before bootstrap.
Figure 5: Depth gains persist with learned readouts. Final and selected-layer scores for CBraMod and REVE on OpenBMI (BA) and N170 (AUROC). Learned readouts average three seeds.
Table 5: Full minus 10% fitting-label effects (percent, paired intervals). Validation pools stay fixed. The second quantity is joint interface utility.

Figure 7: Layer-wise performance under five readouts. Rows identify models and columns identify tasks; colors and line styles share one legend. Scores are participant-average BA (OpenBMI, n = 54) or AUROC (N170/N400, n = 40). LUNA uses the three readouts applicable to its token layout.

Table 7: Cross-fitted forward utility and shuffled residuals of the same dimension (percent; paired 95% intervals). Permutation scores are averaged over 20 seeds within participant before resampling. Both ∆resid and Eresid have positive intervals in 13/15 conditions.

Figure 8: Residual utility across models and feature dimensions. A: PCA200 cross-fitted gains over Final (filled) and shuffled augmentation (open). B: Fixed-layer/readout dimension scan: Selected minus Final and Final + residual minus Final. Native denotes full model-specific dimensions. Intervals are paired participant-bootstrap 95% CIs; the two panels use their respective fitted protocols.

Table 9: Original sensitivity results: augmentation minus Final (%) [95% CI]. Uncompressed ERP features retain all four negative results; Gaussian projections use 200 features per layer. These runs are distinct from the cross-fitted dimension scan.

Table 12: Mapping and task-head capacity at 200 features per layer. Scores and gains are percentages; brackets give paired 95% intervals. BA: OpenBMI; AUROC: N170/N400. The same head family is used within each comparison.
Table 13: Held-out reconstruction diagnostics at PCA200: unweighted means over the five outer-fold mappings. These are reconstruction R2/MSE, not downstream task scores.

Table 15: Source-selected gains across five dataset pairs (%). ∆F : Source minus Final; ∆R: Source minus Random. Sleep uses macro-F1; other tasks use BA. ∗Paired 95% CI includes zero. Full intervals and pair-specific readouts appear in Appendix D.
Table 16: Paired source-selected transfer gains (%) [95% CI] for the five pairs in Table 15.

Table 19: HMC–ISRUC direction-transfer scores: macro-F1 (%) [95% CI], n = 98. Source transformations are fixed. Deletion removes four directions at unit strength; random and shuffled controls average 20 independent bases.

Figure 9: Complete source-direction transfer diagnostics. HMC–ISRUC sleep staging (n = 98), using source-fitted PCA200. A: Final, source-residual augmentation, and Selected macro-F1. B: Intact, rank-four deletion with the target scaler and classifier frozen, and refitted scores for task and random directions. C: Augmentation gains and post-refit excess deletion losses relative to random controls. Random controls average 20 bases; source transformations remain fixed. Intervals are 95% whole-participant bootstrap intervals.
Table 24: Shared-backbone pretraining: absolute scores (%) and fixed-readout depth gains (%) [95% CI], averaged over three paired seeds. The random encoder uses the same backbone.
